reason: This passage explicitly emphasizes hierarchy through multiple interconnected structures: (1) Command authority—Moses directs Joshua to 'choose men and go fight against Amalek,' and 'Joshua did as Moses said to him'; (2) Physical positioning—Moses stands elevated 'on the head of the hill' with the divine rod while Joshua and soldiers fight below; (3) Spiritual authority—Moses's raised hands directly determine military outcome ('when Moses lifted his hand, Israel prevailed; when he lowered it, Amalek prevailed'); (4) Supporting roles—Aaron and Hur support Moses's hands, creating a clear hierarchical structure where they serve his authority; (5) Communicative chain—God speaks to Moses, who then conveys instructions to Joshua; (6) Religious leadership—Moses builds the altar and names it. The entire passage is structured around Moses's supreme authority—both divine delegation and practical command—with Joshua, Aaron, and Hur in subordinate positions exercising obedience.
